editorial:
If you love a good comedy that pokes fun at the Old West, this one is right up your alley. Seth MacFarlane plays Albert, a sheep farmer who is terrible at his job and even worse at standing up for himself. When his girlfriend dumps him for the local mustache shop owner, he meets Anna, a mysterious woman who teaches him how to shoot and stand tall. The catch? She is married to Clinch Leatherwood, one of the most dangerous gunfighters around. The movie is packed with silly jokes, gross-out humor, and plenty of jabs at how deadly life was back then. It feels like a mix between a classic Western and a modern comedy show.

The acting is solid, especially Charlize Theron, who brings real charm to Anna and makes her scenes with Albert feel natural. Liam Neeson is great as the scary villain, and Neil Patrick Harris steals scenes as the smug mustache guy. The pacing moves fast, and the jokes come nonstop, though some land better than others. If you enjoy Seth MacFarlane's style of humor, you will have a blast. If crude jokes are not your thing, you might want to skip it. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Albert faces Clinch in a duel. Instead of shooting him, Albert uses a trick bullet and a hidden mirror to make it look like he won, but Clinch actually survives and tries to kill him. Anna steps in and shoots Clinch dead, saving Albert. Albert and Anna end up together, and he finally stands up for himself. The movie ends with them riding off into the sunset, with Albert joking about how dangerous the West really is. It is a happy ending that wraps up the story with laughs.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crude comedy and Western spoofs
